customerJourneyStories.name: Leaving an overgrown webshop that blocks growth
customerJourneyStories.summary: Illustrative composite based on the published Loods28 case: a growing wholesaler moves from a Magento shop that 'could no longer cope' to Highbiza.

stages.narrative: Order volume and the number of business customers grow quickly; the existing Magento shop becomes slow, extensions break on updates and every change needs an external agency.
Hears about Highbiza through the regional network in Twente and the Achterhoek, and later through the Katapull group site and its ERP sibling Logic4.
Compares the Launch, Core, Prestige and Enterprise packages, asks for a 30-minute demo and checks references; weighs fixed monthly fees and ISO 27001 against the freedom of an open-source shop.
Starts with a test environment on a temporary URL, loads the catalogue and customer groups and runs parallel tests before switching domains over a few months.
The team adds products and seasonal ranges itself in the CMS, trade customers log in for their prices, and new building blocks are switched on as the business grows.
Stays because the shop keeps up with peaks, upgrades package as order volumes rise, and becomes a reference customer quoted on Highbiza and Katapull sites.

customerJourneyStories.name: From a ticket queue to a self-service CMS
customerJourneyStories.summary: Illustrative journey inspired by the published Kroon-Oil case, where marketing ran a tender to replace a custom CMS.

stages.narrative: Social campaigns cannot link to proper landing pages and every homepage change requires a ticket with the old supplier; the team feels neither flexible nor self-reliant.
Marketing and its agency write a tender and invite three suppliers; Highbiza is on the list through its performance references.
Highbiza demonstrates technical performance and a CMS the team can run itself; the company chooses a hybrid of the agency's design and Highbiza's technology.
Several brand sites go live within months on the same technical base; the manager fills the content in the CMS and tests in the staging environment.
Menu and page changes that took weeks now take days; the team publishes campaigns, tunes SEO and adds brands on the same platform.
Stays because further optimisations are cheap and quick, and recommends Highbiza in the published customer story.

customerJourneyStories.name: Joining the webshop and a new ERP as launch customer
customerJourneyStories.summary: Illustrative journey based on the published HR Premium Parts case, which became a launch customer for Highbiza together with Logic4 in 2023.

stages.narrative: The business runs on one laptop, spreadsheets and email; the long-running webshop works at the front but nothing is automated at the back.
A conversation with Highbiza's founder introduces the idea of becoming a launch customer for both the Highbiza shop and the Logic4 ERP.
Weighs the effort of cleaning data against one system for stock, purchasing, customers and invoicing; checks that the long-standing shop can stay.
A finance and control intern inventories data, links product data, customer groups and stock, and configures Logic4 while the shop is reconnected in test.
Dashboards show turnover, product rotation and customer behaviour in real time; orders flow from shop into Logic4 without retyping.
Stays because the shop and ERP grow together within one group and the company now has a structured, scalable base.

customerJourneyStories.summary: Illustrative journey of a trade customer adopting the wholesaler's Highbiza-based B2B shop.

stages.narrative: Waiting on hold to order the usual items and to ask whether a part is in stock costs time on every job.
The wholesaler's rep or an invoice footer announces the new webshop with personal prices and sends a login.
Logs in once to check that the prices match the agreement and that the familiar items are there; compares with ordering by phone.
Places a first small order from the phone; the order confirmation and invoice match what the shop showed.
Uses reorder lists weekly, filters by specification for unfamiliar parts and requests quotes for big jobs online.
Keeps ordering online because it is faster than calling and stock information proves reliable; colleagues in the company get their own logins.

stages.narrative: Looking for a gift and wanting to buy from a trusted local jeweller rather than a marketplace.
Finds the jeweller's webshop through Google search and a social post linking to a collection page.
Checks stock, engraving options, delivery time and payment methods; reassured by the secure checkout and a clear return form.
Places a first order with iDEAL and chooses delivery to a pick-up point.
Comes back for later occasions, collects loyalty points automatically and uses them as a discount.
Keeps buying from the jeweller because the shop is reliable and the points add up; uses the online return form once without friction.
